title: Microsoft Teams: impersonation protection warnings in meetings
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned warnings and the different roadmap and Message Center schedules. No feature-specific setting, default or licence was found; minor corrections should distinguish general Teams licensing, retain the notice's qualifications and remove the checklist instruction for a control missing from the table.

claims.claim: This roadmap feature is impersonation protection for Microsoft Teams meetings.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams: Impersonation Protection for Teams meetings

claims.claim: Teams plans to surface warnings and risk indicators when it detects a potential impersonation attempt.
claims.quote: When Teams detects a potential impersonation attempt, it surfaces warnings and risk indicators

claims.claim: The feature helps users identify potentially deceptive participants and meeting organisers.
claims.quote: Impersonation Protection for Teams meetings helps users identify potentially deceptive participants and meeting organizers.

claims.claim: The warnings help users make decisions when joining or participating in a meeting.
claims.quote: to help users recognize suspicious identities and make more informed decisions when joining or participating in a meeting.

claims.claim: The roadmap and MC1530613 give the same description of the planned behaviour.
claims.quote: When Teams detects a potential impersonation attempt, it surfaces warnings and risk indicators to help users recognize suspicious identities and make more informed decisions when joining or participating in a meeting.

claims.quote: Does the change introduce or modify security controls?Yes. The feature surfaces meeting impersonation warnings and risk indicators to help users make safer meeting decisions.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no page describing this feature at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting impersonation protection warnings risk indicators default admin setting licensing prerequisites detection data; read meeting-policies-overview and returned excerpts. Results describe renaming, messaging protection or third-party synthetic media detection, not this feature.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The default state of meeting impersonation protection is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "meeting impersonation protection" "default" "warnings"; read roadmap, MC1530613, meeting-policies-overview and returned excerpts. No feature-specific default found; 'No immediate admin action is required' does not explicitly state default enforcement.

claims.where: controls[0]: ui and api null; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No tenant or policy switch for meeting impersonation protection is documented on the admin UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams meeting impersonation protection admin center switch PowerShell Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy impersonation default enabled; read meeting-policies-overview and searched full Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference. No switch for this feature found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; summary; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no feature-specific licence requirement is published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' under the standard's product-level licensing rule. Replace the notes with 'Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organisation needs a Teams licence to use Teams. A licence requirement specific to meeting impersonation protection is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access and use this same qualification in Cost and licensing; do not claim Teams Premium is required.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No price or meter specific to meeting impersonation protection is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams meeting impersonation protection licensing price meter Teams license requirement; read Teams Premium licensing, roadmap and MC1530613, plus returned licensing excerpts. No feature-specific price or meter found.

claims.claim: The cited Teams Premium licensing page does not mention meeting impersonation protection.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams meeting impersonation protection licensing price meter Teams license requirement; read the full Microsoft Teams Premium licensing page, including Advanced protection for meetings and licence requirements. Meeting impersonation protection is not listed.

claims.claim: The sources do not describe how Teams detects impersonation for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "meeting impersonation protection" roles prerequisites detection data organizers participants; read roadmap and MC1530613 and search excerpts. The record and notice name potential impersonation but no detection mechanism; synthetic media detection is a separate feature.

claims.claim: The sources do not describe the appearance of a meeting impersonation warning.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting impersonation protection warnings risk indicators default admin setting licensing prerequisites detection data; read roadmap, MC1530613 and returned excerpts. No warning appearance for this feature found.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Users and licences; Open questions
claims.claim: The sources do not specify which meeting roles or participant categories see the warnings.
claims.quote: Searched: "meeting impersonation protection" roles prerequisites detection data organizers participants; read roadmap, MC1530613 and returned excerpts. Both sources say 'users', without allocating warnings to organisers, attendees, guests or external participants.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk; Open questions
claims.claim: No source describes the detection data or its processing location for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "meeting impersonation protection" roles prerequisites detection data organizers participants; read roadmap, MC1530613 and returned excerpts. No data access or processing location for this feature stated; third-party media-processing text describes a different feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity and Autonomy & actions; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The sources describe no autonomous action, participant blocking or admission change beyond warnings and risk indicators.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting impersonation protection warnings risk indicators default admin setting licensing prerequisites detection data; read roadmap, MC1530613 and returned excerpts. Neither record describes blocking, admission changes or automatic actions beyond warnings.

claims.claim: No roles or prerequisites specific to meeting impersonation protection are documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "meeting impersonation protection" roles prerequisites detection data organizers participants; read roadmap, MC1530613, meeting-policies-overview and search excerpts. No feature-specific roles or prerequisites found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling the ParticipantNameChange Teams meeting policy setting stops participants editing display names during meetings.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams enforces this control through the ParticipantNameChange setting in Teams meeting policies. When disabled, participants can't edit their display names during meetings

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: ParticipantNameChange is a separate renaming control, not a documented switch governing this feature's detection or warnings.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams meeting impersonation protection admin center switch PowerShell Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy impersonation default enabled; read the display-name control page and ParticipantNameChange reference. Both describe participant renaming, not detection or warnings.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference lists no impersonation-protection parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: full fetched Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference for impersonat, spoof, suspicious, deceptive and ParticipantNameChange; only ParticipantNameChange matched, described as turning participant renaming on or off. No impersonation-protection parameter found.

claims.claim: The meeting policies overview describes no meeting impersonation protection setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams meeting impersonation protection admin center switch PowerShell Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy impersonation default enabled; read the full Manage meeting and events policies in Microsoft Teams page. It describes policy management, not this setting.

claims.claim: Existing lobby and meeting policy settings control meeting admission.
claims.quote: Who can bypass the lobby is a per-organizer policy and controls whether users join the meeting directly or wait in the lobby for meetings scheduled by the user who is assigned the policy.

claims.claim: A warning identifies potential impersonation rather than proving that the participant is an impersonator.
claims.quote: Meeting Impersonation Protection provides users with additional context to determine whether the people they interact with in Microsoft Teams meetings are who they claim to be.

claims.claim: The sources do not state how frequently warnings appear.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting impersonation protection warnings risk indicators default admin setting licensing prerequisites detection data; read roadmap, MC1530613 and returned excerpts. No warning frequency stated.

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to decide whether to restrict participant renaming, but that control has no table row.
claims.quote: Decide whether to restrict participant renaming through the ParticipantNameChange meeting policy setting described in the controls notes. The table contains only 'Tenant or policy switch for meeting impersonation protection'.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet beginning 'Decide whether to restrict participant renaming'. Keep the existing descriptive controls note; do not add a control row as part of this correction.
